summary: opencode-engos-ai postinstall fetches unpinned platform binary and drops it into system PATH under an unrelated name
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall script runs `npm view opencode-engos-<platform>-<arch> version` to resolve the latest published version of a sibling platform-specific package, then `npm install`s that version and copies the fetched executable into the package's bin directory. It creates root-owned symlinks at /usr/local/bin/innexarcode and /usr/bin/innexarcode, placing the fetched binary on the installer's PATH under a name (`innexarcode`) that does not match the npm package name. The fetched artifact is opaque, resolved via a mutable `latest` pointer (no version pin, no hash/signature verification), and the sibling packages are separately controllable on the registry. The package name closely resembles the legitimate `opencode-ai` project, and the declared optionalDependencies pin (1.18.23) diverges from this package's version (1.20.5), indicating a distinct supply-chain lineage from the project it resembles.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
